title: cost-opt: autotune defaults for batching/caching + quant profiles + unit-econ tooling
author: Asha Patel
description:
Context: customers running production workloads vary widely in seq lengths and QPS; conservative defaults for batching and KV caching cause unnecessary cost for many apps while manual tuning is time-consuming. This PR automates sensible defaults and exposes unit-economics tooling in the Console so customers can see cost/latency tradeoffs when switching quantization profiles or enabling more aggressive batching/caching heuristics.

What this change does: 1) Runtime: introduce an autotune service that determines initial batching and KV cache defaults per model family based on observed seq-length histograms and tail-latency targets; 2) Quant profiles: add an opinionated set of quantization profiles (fp16, int8-qdq, int8-gemmlowp) with calibrated quality penalties and cost estimates surfaced in the Console; 3) Console/UI: add a Unit Economics panel (per-model) showing estimated tokens/sec, cost-per-token, and expected latency at the selected profile and batching policy; 4) Tooling: CLI scripts and an integration test harness to backfill historical metrics and validate rollout.

Design notes: - Autotune runs in the control plane and emits recommended defaults as a config blob; serving nodes fetch and apply recommendations with a safe rollout (start at sample-rate 1% and ramp via canary rules). - Recommendations are bounded by per-customer SLA constraints (explicit overrides preserved) and include a confidence score. - Quant profiles are validated by an offline eval harness (sampled prompts + reference evals) producing a quality delta score; profiles with >2% quality regression are marked experimental and hidden behind opt-in.

Checklist: - [x] Implement autotune service and recommendation API - [x] Add quant profile definitions and offline eval integration - [x] Console Unit Economics panel + cost estimation backend - [x] Backfill scripts for historical metrics - [x] E2E integration tests in perf-canary harness - [x] Docs updates and migration notes

Testing and rollout: initial rollout gated behind feature-flag; ran perf-canary on internal prod traffic for 48h (see CI logs). Metrics: median latency unchanged, p95 latency stable, cost-per-token decreased ~18% on medium-length workloads in canary, int8 profiles reduce GPU memory usage enabling higher batching in many cases.

Notes for reviewers: focus on the safety knobs (override behavior, confidence scoring), how recommendations are surfaced in the Console, and the guardrails for quant profiles. Related Linear: ENG-7123, ENG-7240.

review_thread: Tom Brewer (reviewer): Please confirm SLA override semantics. If a customer pins latency targets, recommendations must not lower batch sizes below the threshold. Also add unit tests for that guardrail.

Asha Patel (author): Added explicit enforcement in runtime/serving/apply_recommendation.go and unit tests in runtime/autotuner/ (see f12b9d0). Recommendations now include 'min_latency_slo' and we respect customer overrides.
Ravi Kapoor (reviewer): The quant profiles look good. Can we make the experimental profiles opt-in in the Console (checkbox) and default to hidden?

Asha Patel (author): Experimental profiles are now behind 'Show experimental quant profiles' toggle in UnitEconomicsPanel.tsx and hidden by default. Offline eval marks experimental=true for profiles with quality delta >1.5%.
Monica Li (reviewer): Suggest we surface the confidence score more prominently in the Console and include a link to the backfill script so operators can reproduce recommendations locally.
Asha Patel (author): Moved confidence score to the top of the panel and added backfill script README link.
release_notes: Automated defaults for batching/KV caching based on workload histograms; opinionated quantization profiles surfaced in Console; Unit Economics panel to preview cost/latency tradeoffs; safe rollout and operator docs.
notes: Canary ran on internal fleet for 48h; observed ~18% cost reduction for median workloads. Ops: feature-flag rollout; admins can roll back recommendations per model. Plan: gradual rollout to 10% customers over 2 weeks, monitor quality regressions and p95 latency.
testing_instructions: Enable feature flag 'cost_opt_autotune' in Console -> Admin -> Feature flags. Run tools/backfill_metrics/backfill.sh with date range to seed recommendations. Verify Unit Economics panel populates and check canary metrics in perf-canary dashboard.
